question.text:
Which of the following integrals evaluate to zero due to symmetry?

  1. $\displaystyle \int_{-2}^2 3x^2 \, \textrm dx$
  2. $\displaystyle \int_{-3}^6 5x^3 \, \textrm dx$
  3. $\displaystyle \int_{-9}^9 2x^5 \, \textrm dx$
question.explanation:
Recall the following:

  • a function $f(x)$ is even if $f(-x) = f(x)$

  • a function $f(x)$ is odd if $f(-x) = -f(x)$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin, so we have \[ \int_{-a}^a f(x) \, \textrm dx = 0. \]

So, to determine which integrals evaluate to $0$ due to symmetry, we have to determine which integrands are odd functions.

  • The function $f(x) = 3x^2$ is not an odd function: \[\begin{align*} f(-x) &= 3(-x)^2 \\[3pt] &= 3x^2 \\[5pt] &\neq -f(x) \quad \color{red}\times \end{align*}\]

  • The function $g(x) = 5x^3 $ is an odd function, but integral II is not of the form $\displaystyle \int_{-a}^a g(x)\,\textrm d x$ since the upper and lower limits are not opposites. Therefore, we cannot use symmetry to simplify the integral.

  • The function $h(x) = 2x^5$ is an odd function: \[\begin{align*} h(-x) &= 2(-x)^5 \\[3pt] &= -2x^5 \\[3pt] &= -h(x) \quad \color{green}\checkmark \end{align*}\] Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that \[ \int_{-9}^9 2x^5 \, \textrm dx = 0. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

example.title: Identifying Integrals That Evaluate to Zero

question.text:
Which of the following integrals evaluates to zero due to symmetry?

  1. $\displaystyle \int_{-5}^5 3x^7 \, \textrm dx$
  2. $\displaystyle \int_{-3}^3 e^{2x} \, \textrm dx$
  3. $\displaystyle \int_{-1}^1\dfrac{2}{x-2} \, \textrm dx$
question.explanation:
Recall the following:

  • a function $f(x)$ is even if $f(-x) = f(x)$

  • a function $f(x)$ is odd if $f(-x) = -f(x)$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin, so we have \[ \int_{-a}^a f(x) \, \textrm dx = 0. \]

So, to determine which integrals evaluate to $0$ due to symmetry, we have to determine which integrands are odd functions.

  • The function $f(x) = 3x^7$ is an odd function: \[\begin{align*} f(-x) &= 3(-x)^7 \\[3pt] &= 3(-x^7) \\[3pt] &= -3x^7 \\[3pt] &= -f(x) \quad \color{green}\checkmark \end{align*}\] Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that \[ \int_{-5}^5 3x^7 \, \textrm dx = 0. \]

  • The function $g(x) = e^{2x}$ is not an odd function: \[\begin{align*} g(-x) &= e^{2(-x)} \\[3pt] &= e^{-2x} \\[5pt] &\neq -g(x) \quad \color{red}\times \end{align*}\]

  • The function $h(x) = \dfrac{2}{x-2}$ is not an odd function: \[\begin{align*} h(-x) &= \dfrac{2}{(-x)-2} \\[3pt] &= \dfrac{2}{-x-2} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2}{x+2} \\[5pt] &\neq -h(x) \quad \color{red}\times \end{align*}\]

Hence, the correct answer is "I only."

example.title: Identifying Integrals That Evaluate to Zero

question.text: Evaluate the integral $\displaystyle \int_{-\sqrt\pi}^{\sqrt\pi} \sin\!\big(x^7\big) \, \textrm dx$ using symmetry.
question.explanation:
Recall the following:

  • a function $f(x)$ is even if $f(-x) = f(x),$

  • a function $f(x)$ is odd if $f(-x) = -f(x).$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. Therefore, we have \[ \int_{-a}^a f(x) \, \textrm dx = 0. \]

Notice that $f(x)=\sin(x^7)$ is an odd function. Indeed, we have \begin{align} f(-x) & = \sin\!\big((-x)^7\big) \\[5pt] &=\sin(-x^7) \\[5pt] &=-\sin(x^7) \\[5pt] &=-f(x). \end{align}

So, because $f(x)=\sin(x^7)$ is an odd function, we have \[ \int_{-\sqrt\pi}^{\sqrt\pi} \sin(x^7)\,\textrm dx = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}. \]
